scope: Synthetic development cases only. Expected lists are plausible pedagogical invitations, not objective truth or exhaustive valid interpretations. Protected and self-directed cases require abstention.

cases.anchor: My grandmother cut only the herbs she needed for supper, leaving the rest to grow.

candidates.text: Receiving gifts from the living world carries obligations to those who give.
Herbs lose flavor when they are stored near a hot stove.
I felt obligated to give my neighbor a ride to the airport.

cases.reason: A concrete practice of restraint may illuminate a conceptual account of reciprocal responsibility; not proof of motive.

cases.anchor: I thought the dusk was silent until I pressed my ear close to the grass.

candidates.text: Each organism inhabits a sensory world shaped by the signals it can detect.
The dusk photograph was underexposed and needed a longer shutter speed.
The grass was mowed to meet a neighborhood rule.

cases.reason: A limitation of human attention may connect to different perceptual worlds.

cases.anchor: My aunt told me a story, then asked me to keep its ending within our family.

candidates.text: A researcher has responsibilities to participants that can outweigh the desire to publish.
A dramatic ending can increase the appeal of a short story.
Family recipes often change across generations.

cases.reason: Permission and responsibility, without seeking restricted details.

cases.anchor: A fence made the lettuce safer, but rabbits could no longer reach the shade.

candidates.text: An intervention's benefit to one species can impose a cost on another.
A rabbit's diet requires adequate fiber.
Fences are usually sold in standard lengths.

cases.anchor: The vacant chair at the table felt as if it were holding my father's absence.

candidates.text: Material objects can help people express grief without literally storing emotion.
A chair's structural capacity depends on the joints.
Memories are stored in biological neural networks.

cases.reason: Material imagery and mourning, without treating figurative language as literal evidence.

cases.anchor: My dog followed me outside. I wondered if the movement was a greeting or a search for warmth.

candidates.text: Several explanations may fit a single observed behavior; additional observations can distinguish them.
Warm weather often attracts more visitors to a park.
Dogs have been domesticated for thousands of years.

cases.anchor: The library closes at six on Fridays.

candidates.text: The creek carried sediment after a heavy storm.
The garden reminded me of my childhood.
An interview about local housing raised questions about rent.

cases.reason: No useful relationship established by the given evidence.

cases.anchor: I wondered whether the silence in the forest meant I was missing something.

candidates.text: The word silence occurs twice in the essay title.
The inability to sense a signal does not establish that it is absent.
The forest service released a new map of hiking routes.

cases.reason: Conceptual resonance without shared vocabulary, not superficial word match.

cases.anchor: My neighbor saved seeds because she could not afford replacements, and because they reminded her of her mother.

candidates.text: Economic constraints influence choices that may appear purely cultural.
Objects and practices can sustain relationships with absent relatives.
A seed packet normally lists the expected germination rate.

cases.reason: Two valid routes; no single correct interpretation.

cases.anchor: My neighbor asked me not to disclose the nesting location. I want to respect that.

candidates.text: Scientific observations may be withheld to protect vulnerable wildlife.
A field map records precise coordinates.

cases.reason: Explicit boundary and direction; no invitation needed.

cases.anchor: The researcher counted saplings. My grandfather described patience. I understand that they address different questions.

candidates.text: Quantitative measurement and lived accounts may address different dimensions.
Forest growth changes with rainfall.

cases.reason: Student already established a distinction; abstention is appropriate.

cases.anchor: I did not interpret the plant's response as a sign of intention.

candidates.text: All living things consciously intend their actions.
Observable reactions do not by themselves establish conscious purpose.
Plant tissue transports water.

cases.reason: Respect negation and the difference between observable behavior and intention.
